note: Kepler two-body motion is analytic: position at any time t comes from a closed-form solve of Kepler's equation, so any client can evaluate state at any t without stepping (random access, no drift, cheap, identical inputs give the same output up to the solver's tolerance). In the restricted problem the primaries can still be put on analytic Kepler orbits (the quoted model prescribes m(t), e(t)), but the ship's trajectory has no closed form and must be stepped; error then accumulates (phase error grows, symplectic bound applies to energy only, and only for constant step as Yoshida states; the Lee-Duncan-Levison abstract notes that naively varying the step destroys the property). Race consequences: ship state is a function of the whole input history, so all clients need fixed dt and identical inputs/ordering or an authoritative server; track checkpoints/ranking cannot be computed in closed form for the ship; if bodies are N>2 mutually interacting, even the bodies are not analytic. Body count, dt and error budget are still unspecified in the brief (C-194); here dt=0.001 with 3 sources gave 1e-12 -> 6e-8 in 1e5 steps.
